style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: After Psalm 22, the psalm the New Testament quotes most about the sufferings of Christ. It opens underwater -- save me, the waters have come up to my neck -- and keeps sinking: deep mire with no floor, floods overflowing, a throat worn raw from calling, eyes worn out from watching for God. The griefs are specific and mostly social. Hated without cause by more people than he has hairs; made to give back what he never stole; a stranger to his own brothers; mocked by the men in the gate and made the drinking song of the town -- all of it because zeal for God's house has eaten him alive, and the insults aimed at God landed on him. He never pretends to be innocent in general -- You know my foolishness, and my guilt is not hidden from You -- but he is innocent in this, and his one fear is that his disgrace will embarrass everyone who waits for God. Then the two verses the Gospels could not miss: they gave me gall for food, and vinegar for my thirst; and I looked for pity and found none, for comforters and found nobody. The imprecation that follows is the hardest in the Psalter, and the apostles applied it -- Peter to Judas, Paul to unbelieving Israel. But the psalm ends singing: I will praise God's name with a song, and He prefers it to an ox with horns and hooves. God will save Zion; the seed of His servants will inherit it; and those who love His name will live there.

1.text: For the choir director, to 'Lilies.' Of David. Save me, O God, for the waters have come up to my neck!
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach] upon Shoshannim [shushan -- lilies], A Psalm of David. Save [yasha] me, O God [Elohim]; for the waters [mayim] are come [bo] in unto my soul [nephesh].
1.notes: hoshieni Elohim ki bau mayim ad-naphesh (H3467, H430, H935, H4325, H5315): save me, God, for the waters have come up to the NEPHESH -- the throat, the neck, which is the word's concrete sense before it means soul: water at the windpipe. Shoshannim (H7799), 'lilies', is a tune name (also Psalm 45, 80). After Psalm 22, the psalm the New Testament quotes most often of Christ's sufferings.

2.text: I have sunk in deep mud where there is no footing; I have come into deep water, and the current has swept over me.
2.amp: I sink in deep ['the mire of depth', yaven, the KJV margin] mire, where there is no standing [maamad -- footing]: I am come [bo] into deep ['depth of waters', maim, the KJV margin] waters [mayim], where the floods overflow me.
2.notes: tabati bi-yeven metsulah ve-en maomad (H2883, H3121, H4688, H4613): I have sunk in the mire of the depth -- the margin's literal -- and there is no maamad, no place to stand; bati be-maamaqqe-mayim ve-shibbolet shetaphatni (H4615, H7641, H7857): I have come into the depths of water and the CURRENT has swept me -- shibbolet, a flowing stream (and the password of Judges 12:6). Jeremiah in the cistern's mud (Jeremiah 38:6) is the nearest picture.

3.text: I am worn out from calling; my throat is scorched; my eyes have failed while I wait for my God.
3.amp: I am weary [yaga] of my crying [qara]: my throat is dried [charar]: mine eyes [ayin] fail [kalah] while I wait [yachal] for my God [Elohim].
3.notes: yagati be-qori nichar geroni (H3021, H7121, H2787, H1627): I am WORN OUT with my calling; my throat is scorched -- charar, the burning of Psalm 102:3's bones; kalu enai meyachel l-Elohai (H3615, H5869, H3176, H430): my eyes are spent, WAITING for my God -- yachal, hope as watching. Not a man who has stopped praying: a man whose voice and sight have given out first.

4.text: More than the hairs of my head are those who hate me for nothing; mighty are those who would silence me, my enemies for a lie -- what I never stole, I am made to give back.
4.amp: They that hate [sane] me without a cause [chinnam] are more than the hairs of mine head [rosh]: they that would destroy me, being mine enemies [oyeb] wrongfully [sheqer], are mighty [atsam]: then I restored [shub] that which I took not away [gazal].
4.notes: rabbu mi-saarot roshi soneai chinnam (H7231, H8185, H7218, H8130, H2600): more than the hairs of my head are those hating me CHINNAM -- for nothing, gratis: the word Jesus applies to Himself from this psalm and Psalm 35:19 (John 15:25); atsemu matsmitai oyebai sheqer (H6105, H6789, H341, H8267): mighty are those who would silence me, my enemies falsely; asher lo-gazalti az ashib (H1497, H7725): what I did not ROB, then I restore -- the proverb of a man forced to repay a theft he never committed.

5.text: O God, You Yourself know my foolishness, and my guilt is not hidden from You.
5.amp: O God [Elohim], You know [yada] my foolishness [ivvelet]; and my sins ['guiltiness', ashmah, the KJV margin] are not hid [kachad] from You.
5.notes: Elohim attah yadata le-ivvalti (H430, H3045, H200): God, YOU know my folly -- the same ivvelet Psalm 38:5 blamed for the wounds; ve-ashmotai mimmekha lo-nikhchadu (H819, H3582): and my guiltinesses -- the margin's word -- are not concealed from You. The psalm's honesty: hated without cause (v. 4) is not the same as sinless, and the sufferer says so. It is one reason the New Testament quotes the psalm's sufferings of Christ without quoting this verse of Him.

6.text: Let not those who wait for You be shamed through me, O Lord GOD of hosts; let not those who seek You be humiliated because of me, O God of Israel.
6.amp: Let not them that wait [qavah] on You, O Lord [Adonai] GOD of hosts [tsaba], be ashamed [bosh] for my sake: let not those that seek [baqash] You be confounded [kalam] for my sake, O God [Elohim] of Israel [Yisrael].
6.notes: al-yeboshu bi qovekha Adonai YHWH tsebaot (H954, H6960, H136, H6635): let not those WAITING for You be shamed through me, Lord GOD of armies; al-yikkalmu bi mebaqshekha Elohe Yisrael (H3637, H1245, H430, H3478): let not Your seekers be humiliated because of me. His deepest fear is not his own disgrace but that it will discredit everyone else who trusts God -- the anxiety of every public believer under attack.

7.text: For it is for Your sake that I have carried reproach, that humiliation has covered my face.
7.amp: Because for Your sake I have borne [nasa] reproach [cherpah]; shame [kelimmah] has covered [kasah] my face [panim].
7.notes: ki-alekha nasati cherpah (H5375, H2781): because for YOU I have CARRIED reproach -- nasa, the bearing-verb of Isaiah 53:4's griefs; kissetah khelimmah phanai (H3680, H3639): humiliation has covered my face. The cause is named: the trouble is not accidental, it is the cost of association with God (cf. Romans 15:3, which quotes verse 9 for exactly this).

8.text: I have become a stranger to my brothers, a foreigner to my mother's sons.
8.amp: I am become a stranger [zur] unto my brethren [ach], and an alien [nokri] unto my mother's [em] children [ben].
8.notes: muzar hayiti le-echai (H2114, H251): I have become ESTRANGED to my brothers -- ve-nokhri li-bne immi (H5237, H1121, H517): a foreigner to my mother's sons. Not distant relatives: the same womb. John 7:5 says the same of one Man's brothers, who did not believe in Him.

9.text: For zeal for Your house has eaten me up, and the insults of those who insult You have fallen on me.
9.amp: For the zeal [qinah] of Your house [bayith] has eaten me up [akal]; and the reproaches [cherpah] of them that reproached [charaph] You are fallen [naphal] upon me.
9.notes: ki-qinat betekha akhalatni (H7068, H1004, H398): for zeal for Your house has DEVOURED me -- qinah, the jealousy-word, a fire that consumes the one who carries it; ve-cherpot chorephekha naphelu alai (H2781, H2778, H5307): and the insults of those insulting You have fallen on me. The disciples remembered the first half when Jesus cleared the temple (John 2:17); Paul quotes the second half of Christ in Romans 15:3. The whole psalm turns on this verse: the suffering is transferred, and it is God who was the target.

10.text: When I wept and humbled my soul with fasting, that itself became insults against me.
10.amp: When I wept [bakah], and chastened my soul [nephesh] with fasting, that was to my reproach [cherpah].
10.notes: va-ebkeh ba-tsom naphshi (H1058, H6685, H5315): I wept, with fasting, my soul -- the standard signs of repentance; va-tehi la-charaphot li (H2781): and it became insults for me. Piety itself read as pretension: the mockery of a man who takes God seriously in public (cf. Matthew 6:16-18 for the other danger).

11.text: I made sackcloth my clothing, and I became a byword to them.
11.amp: I made [natan] sackcloth also my garment; and I became a proverb [mashal -- byword] to them.
11.notes: va-ettenah lebushi saq (H5414, H3830, H8242): I made my garment sackcloth -- the coarse mourning cloth; va-ehi lahem le-mashal (H4912): and I became to them a mashal, a byword -- the fate Deuteronomy 28:37 lists as a curse, here landing on the faithful man instead.

12.text: Those who sit in the gate talk about me, and I am the drinking song of the drunkards.
12.amp: They that sit in [yashab] the gate [shaar] speak [siach] against me; and I was the song [neginah] of the drunkards ['drinkers of strong drink', shekar, the KJV margin].
12.notes: yasichu bi yoshebe shaar (H7878, H3427, H8179): those SITTING IN THE GATE talk about me -- the gate is the courthouse and the town council (Ruth 4:1): the respectable men; u-neginot shote shekhar (H5058, H8354, H7941): and the songs of the 'drinkers of strong drink', the margin's literal. Top and bottom of the town, agreed on one joke.

13.text: But as for me, my prayer is to You, O LORD, at an acceptable time; O God, in the abundance of Your covenant love, answer me in the truth of Your salvation.
13.amp: But as for me, my prayer [tephillah] is unto You, O LORD [YHWH], in an acceptable [ratson] time [et]: O God [Elohim], in the multitude [rob] of Your mercy [chesed -- covenant love] hear [anah -- answer] me, in the truth [emeth] of Your salvation [yesha].
13.notes: va-ani tephillati-lekha YHWH et ratson (H8605, H3068, H6256, H7522): but I -- my prayer is to You, LORD, at a time of RATSON: favor, acceptance, the word for a sacrifice God receives; Paul's 'accepted time' in 2 Corinthians 6:2 comes from the same idea in Isaiah 49:8; Elohim be-rob-chasdekha aneni be-emet yishekha (H430, H7230, H2617, H6030, H571, H3468): God, in the abundance of Your chesed answer me, in the truth of Your salvation.

14.text: Rescue me from the mud, and do not let me sink; let me be rescued from those who hate me, and out of the deep water.
14.amp: Deliver [natsal] me out of the mire, and let me not sink: let me be delivered [natsal] from them that hate [sane] me, and out of the deep [maamaq] waters [mayim].
14.notes: hatsileni mi-tit ve-al-etbaa (H5337, H2916, H2883): rescue me from the tit, the clay-mud, and let me not SINK -- verse 2's verb; innatselah mi-sonai u-mi-maamaqqe mayim (H8130, H4615, H4325): let me be rescued from my haters and from the water's depths. Verses 14-15 pray the metaphors of verses 1-2 back to God, item by item.

15.text: Do not let the current of water sweep me away, or the deep swallow me down, or the well shut its mouth over me.
15.amp: Let not the waterflood [mayim] overflow me, neither let the deep [metsulah] swallow me up [bala], and let not the pit [beer] shut [atar] her mouth [peh] upon me.
15.notes: al-tishtepheni shibbolet mayim (H7857, H7641, H4325): let the water's CURRENT not sweep me; ve-al-tibhlaeni metsulah (H1104, H4688): let the deep not SWALLOW me -- bala, Jonah's fish and Korah's ground; ve-al-tetar alai beer piha (H332, H875, H6310): and let the well not SHUT its mouth over me -- the cistern's stone rolled back into place, and the man still inside.

16.text: Answer me, O LORD, for Your covenant love is good; according to the abundance of Your compassion, turn to me.
16.amp: Hear [anah -- answer] me, O LORD [YHWH]; for Your lovingkindness [chesed -- covenant love] is good [tov]: turn [panah] unto me according to the multitude [rob] of Your tender mercies [rachamim].
16.notes: aneni YHWH ki-tov chasdekha (H6030, H3068, H2896, H2617): answer me, LORD, because Your chesed is GOOD -- the ground of the appeal is God's character, not the sufferer's case; ke-rob rachamekha peneh elai (H7230, H7356, H6437): according to the abundance of Your rachamim -- womb-compassion -- TURN to me.

17.text: Do not hide Your face away from Your servant; things are narrow for me -- be quick, answer me.
17.amp: And hide [satar] not Your face [panim] from Your servant [ebed]; for I am in trouble [tsarar]: hear ['make haste to hear me', maher, the KJV margin] me speedily.
17.notes: ve-al-taster panekha me-abdekha (H5641, H6440, H5650): do not hide Your face from Your servant; ki-tsar-li maher aneni (H6887, H4118, H6030): for it is NARROW to me -- HURRY, answer me, the margin's 'make haste to hear me'. The two-word emergency of Psalm 102:2.

18.text: Come near to my soul; redeem it; ransom me because of my enemies.
18.amp: Draw nigh [qarab] unto my soul [nephesh], and redeem [gaal] it: deliver [padah -- ransom] me because of mine enemies [oyeb].
18.notes: qorbah el-naphshi gealah (H7126, H5315, H1350): COME NEAR to my soul, REDEEM it -- gaal, the kinsman-redeemer's verb: the next of kin who buys back a relative sold into debt (Leviticus 25:48-49), which is what the estranged man of verse 8 needs most; lemaan oyebai pedeni (H6299, H341): because of my enemies, ransom me.

19.text: You Yourself know my reproach, my shame, and my humiliation; all my adversaries are in front of You.
19.amp: You have known [yada] my reproach [cherpah], and my shame [bosheth], and my dishonour [kelimmah]: mine adversaries [tsarar] are all before You.
19.notes: attah yadata cherpati u-boshti u-khelimmati (H3045, H2781, H1322, H3639): YOU know my reproach, my shame, my humiliation -- the three shame-words of the psalm gathered in one line and handed over; negdekha kol-tsorerai: before You are all my adversaries. He does not have to produce the list; God is already looking at it.

20.text: Reproach has broken my heart, and I am sick; I looked for sympathy, and there was none, and for comforters, and I found nobody.
20.amp: Reproach [cherpah] has broken [shabar] my heart [leb]; and I am full of heaviness: and I looked [qavah] for some to take pity ['to lament with me', nud, the KJV margin], but there was none; and for comforters [nacham], but I found [matsa] none.
20.notes: cherpah shaberah libbi va-anushah (H2781, H7665, H3820): reproach has BROKEN my heart and I am sick -- anash, incurable, Jeremiah's word for a wound that will not close (Jeremiah 17:9); va-aqavveh la-nud va-ayin (H6960, H5110): I waited for someone 'to lament with me', the margin's literal, and there was none; ve-la-menachamim ve-lo matsati (H5162, H4672): and for comforters, and I found none. Gethsemane's sleeping friends (Mark 14:37) and the mockery at the cross are where the church has always heard this verse.

21.text: They put gall in my food, and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
21.amp: They gave [natan] me also gall [rosh -- poison] for my meat; and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink [shaqah].
21.notes: va-yittenu be-baruti rosh (H5414, H1267, H7219): they gave into my food ROSH -- a bitter poisonous plant, gall (Deuteronomy 29:18; Lamentations 3:19); ve-li-tsmai yashquni chomets (H6772, H8248, H2558): and for my thirst they made me drink chomets, sour wine. All four Gospels record both halves at Golgotha (Matthew 27:34, 48; Mark 15:23, 36; Luke 23:36; John 19:28-30, which says Jesus spoke 'that the scripture might be fulfilled').

22.text: Let their own table before them become a snare, and to those at ease, a trap.
22.amp: Let their table [shulchan] become a snare before [panim] them: and that which should have been for their welfare [shalom], let it become a trap [moqesh].
22.notes: yehi shulchanam liphnehem le-phach (H7979, H6440, H6341): let their TABLE before them become a trap -- the place of fellowship and security turned into the snapping net; ve-li-shlomim le-moqesh (H7965, H4170): and for those at peace, a snare. Paul quotes verses 22-23 in Romans 11:9-10 of Israel's hardening -- and then argues that the hardening is temporary and salvation goes to the nations through it.

23.text: Let their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and make their loins shake continually.
23.amp: Let their eyes [ayin] be darkened, that they see [raah] not; and make their loins continually [tamid] to shake.
23.notes: techshakhnah enehem me-reot (H2821, H5869, H7200): let their eyes go DARK from seeing; u-mothnehem tamid hamad (H4975, H8548, H4571): and make their loins continually TOTTER -- the hips giving way, a body that cannot carry itself. Blindness and collapse: the two things Paul saw in his own nation's refusal (Romans 11:8-10), and he had been blind himself for three days.

24.text: Pour out Your indignation on them, and let Your burning anger overtake them.
24.amp: Pour out [shaphak] Your indignation upon them, and let Your wrathful [charon] anger [aph] take hold of them.
24.notes: shephakh-alehem zamekha (H8210, H2195): POUR OUT on them Your indignation -- shaphak, the verb for pouring out blood and pouring out the soul; va-charon appekha yassigem (H2740, H639, H5381): and let the burning of Your anger OVERTAKE them -- nasag, to catch up with someone running away. The psalm's imprecations are the hardest in the Psalter, and they are prayers, not plans: everything asked for is left in God's hands.

25.text: Let their encampment be desolate; let no one live in their tents.
25.amp: Let their habitation ['their palace', tirah, the KJV margin] be desolate [shamem]; and let none dwell ['let there not be a dweller', yashab, the KJV margin] in their tents [ohel].
25.notes: tehi-tiratam neshammah (H2918, H8074): let their tirah -- encampment, or the margin's 'palace' -- be DESOLATE; be-oholehem al-yehi yoshev (H168, H3427): in their tents let there be no dweller, the margin's literal. Peter quotes this verse of Judas' field in Acts 1:20, joined to Psalm 109:8 -- the apostles read the psalm as speaking about the betrayer of the Man it describes.

26.text: For they hound the one You have struck, and they retell the pain of those You have wounded.
26.amp: For they persecute [radaph] him whom You have smitten [nakah]; and they talk [saphar] to the grief [makob] of those ['thy wounded', chalal, the KJV margin] whom You have wounded.
26.notes: ki-attah asher-hikkita radaphu (H5221, H7291): for the one YOU struck, they hound -- ve-el-makob chalalekha yesapperu (H4341, H2491, H5608): and of the pain of 'Your wounded', the margin's literal, they RECOUNT. The charge is precise: kicking a man God is already disciplining, and making a story of it (cf. Zechariah 1:15).

27.text: Charge guilt on top of the guilt they have, and let them have no entrance into Your righteousness.
27.amp: Add [natan] iniquity [avon] unto their iniquity ['punishment of iniquity', avon, the KJV margin]: and let them not come [bo] into Your righteousness [tsedaqah].
27.notes: tenah-avon al-avonam (H5414, H5771): give guilt on top of their guilt -- or, as the margin reads avon, punishment upon punishment; ve-al-yabou be-tsidqatekha (H935, H6666): and let them not enter into Your righteousness -- not into acquittal. The line the church cannot pray as it stands toward any person, because it prays the opposite (Luke 23:34); it stands in Scripture as the just verdict that grace suspends.

28.text: Let them be blotted out of the scroll of the living, and not enrolled with the righteous.
28.amp: Let them be blotted [machah] out of the book [sepher] of the living [chay], and not be written [kathab] with the righteous [tsaddiq].
28.notes: yimmachu mi-sepher chayyim (H4229, H5612, H2416): let them be WIPED from the book of the living -- machah, the erasure of Exodus 32:32-33, where Moses offers to be blotted out himself; ve-im tsaddiqim al-yikkatebu (H6662, H3789): and with the righteous let them not be written. The register of Psalm 87:6, read from the other side (cf. Philippians 4:3; Revelation 20:15).

29.text: But I am afflicted and in pain; let Your salvation, O God, set me up on high.
29.amp: But I am poor [ani -- afflicted] and sorrowful [kaab]: let Your salvation [yeshuah], O God [Elohim], set me up on high [sagab].
29.notes: va-ani ani ve-khoeb (H6041, H3510): but I am afflicted and in PAIN -- kaab, the ache of Psalm 38:17; yeshuatekha Elohim tesaggebeni (H3444, H430, H7682): let Your salvation, God, SET ME HIGH -- sagab, to put out of reach, on a cliff the enemy cannot climb (Psalm 20:1). The imprecations end; the psalm's own request is one line long.

30.text: I will praise God's name with a song, and I will magnify Him with thanksgiving.
30.amp: I will praise [halal] the name [shem] of God [Elohim] with a song [shir], and will magnify [gadal] Him with thanksgiving [todah].
30.notes: ahalelah shem-Elohim be-shir (H1984, H8034, H430, H7892): I will PRAISE the name of God with a song; va-agaddelennu be-todah (H1431, H8426): and I will MAGNIFY Him with thanksgiving. The turn every lament makes, and this one makes it while still in the water: the vow is present tense.

31.text: That will suit the LORD better than an ox, better than a bull grown out to horn and hoof.
31.amp: This also shall please [yatab] the LORD [YHWH] better [yatab] than an ox or bullock that has horns and hoofs.
31.notes: ve-titab la-YHWH mi-shor par maqrin maphris (H3190, H3068, H7794, H6499, H7160, H6536): and it will please the LORD better than an ox, a bull HORNED and hoofed -- the full-grown, unblemished, maximum offering. The song of a poor man outweighs the biggest animal on the altar: Psalm 50:14 and 51:17 in one line (cf. Hebrews 13:15).

32.text: The humble see it and are glad. You who go seeking God -- let your heart live!
32.amp: The humble ['meek', anav, the KJV margin] shall see [raah] this, and be glad [samach]: and your heart [lebab] shall live [chayah] that seek [darash] God [Elohim].
32.notes: rau anavim yismachu (H7200, H6035, H8055): the humble have SEEN and are glad -- the anavim, the afflicted class of Psalm 9:12; doreshe Elohim vi-chi lebabkhem (H1875, H430, H2421, H3824): you who SEEK God -- let your heart LIVE. His rescue is their oxygen: verse 6's fear that he would shame them, answered.

33.text: For the LORD listens to the needy, and He does not despise His own prisoners.
33.amp: For the LORD [YHWH] hears [shama] the poor [ebyon], and despises [bazah] not His prisoners [asir].
33.notes: ki-shomea el-ebyonim YHWH (H8085, H34, H3068): for the LORD LISTENS to the needy; ve-et-asirav lo bazah (H615, H959): and His prisoners He does not despise -- 'His' prisoners: the chained still belong to Him, which is what Joseph, Jeremiah, and Paul in turn discovered (cf. Ephesians 3:1).

34.text: Let the heavens praise Him, and the earth, the seas and every creeping thing in them.
34.amp: Let the heaven [shamayim] and earth [eretz] praise [halal] Him, the seas [yam], and every thing that moves ['creepeth', ramas, the KJV margin] therein.
34.notes: yehaleluhu shamayim va-arets (H1984, H8064, H776): let heaven and earth praise Him; yammim ve-khol-romes bam (H3220, H7430): the seas and everything CREEPING in them, the margin's verb. The water that was drowning him in verse 2 is drafted into the choir.

35.text: For God will save Zion and build the cities of Judah, and they will settle there and possess it.
35.amp: For God [Elohim] will save [yasha] Zion [Tsiyyon], and will build [banah] the cities [ir] of Judah [Yehudah]: that they may dwell [yashab] there, and have it in possession [yarash].
35.notes: ki Elohim yoshia Tsiyyon ve-yibneh are Yehudah (H430, H3467, H6726, H1129, H5892, H3063): for God will SAVE Zion and BUILD Judah's cities; ve-yashebu sham vi-reshuha (H3427, H3423): and they will settle there and possess it. The individual sufferer's psalm ends as a national promise: what God does for one drowning man He does for a ruined country.

36.text: The offspring of His servants will inherit it, and those who love His name will live in it.
36.amp: The seed [zera] also of His servants [ebed] shall inherit [nachal] it: and they that love [ahab] His name [shem] shall dwell [shakan] therein.
36.notes: ve-zera abadav yinchaluha (H2233, H5650, H5157): the seed of His servants will INHERIT it; ve-ohabe shemo yishkenu-bah (H157, H8034, H7931): and the lovers of His name will dwell in it. The psalm that began with a man sinking alone ends with a settled people, and the qualification for citizenship is love of the Name -- which is what the sufferer had, and what it cost him (v. 9).
